market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note only — no directional macro or index-level view is provided in this edition.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 expected), but the quality was low — the upside was driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1% expectation, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted positive sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's footprint into high-growth robotics and AI-driven vision markets.

MillerKnoll posted a solid FQ1 EPS beat (53 cents vs. 36 cents expected), and notably would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind — ex-refunds EPS was 42 cents versus the 36-cent consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the $943.2 million estimate, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership transition event with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents expected) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate, despite revenue coming in slightly above consensus at $2.311 billion versus $2.17 billion expected. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog, though the company will not provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout that positions VK2735 as a competitive entry in the high-stakes obesity and metabolic disease drug market. The positive efficacy data is a major catalyst for the stock.

sectors: The RV industry faces continued macro headwinds per THOR management — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring consumer discretionary spending and keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a fresh bullish data point from Viking's VK2735 trial results. Cognex's RealSense acquisition signals continued corporate investment in Physical AI and robotic vision technology.
tts_summary:
Good morning. Today's note is a pure earnings and company news edition — there's no broad macro or index-level commentary this morning, so let's go straight to the names that matter.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth fiscal quarter earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents — but the quality of that beat is questionable. The upside was largely driven by tariff refunds, which provided a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets murkier. Domestic same-store sales came in at plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. This is a mixed print — beat on the headline, miss on the quality.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI applications — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 and a half million. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic expansion into high-growth robotics and AI vision, and the deal reads bullish for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll delivered a clean earnings beat — 53 cents versus the 36-cent consensus — and management was clear that even without tariff refund help, they would have beaten at 42 cents. That's encouraging. Sales did miss, declining 3.3% organically, though orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed modestly while earnings per share guidance held firm. Mixed but leaning constructive given the earnings quality.

THOR Industries missed on earnings — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well short of the 13.85% estimate. Management's tone was cautious, blaming interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation for suppressing consumer demand during the critical selling season. The bright spots: dealer inventories are healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. Mostly a bear print with a few offsets.

Finally, the big mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. The company reported positive trial data for its GLP-1 weight loss drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. That's a headline number that will get attention across the obesity drug space. Shares are spiking in pre-market. This is a significant clinical win and keeps Viking firmly in the conversation as a serious competitor in one of the most watched drug categories on the market.

Bottom line for today: no macro directional call in this edition. The action is in the individual names — watch Viking for GLP-1 sector read-through, and treat AutoZone's beat with appropriate skepticism given the quality issues.
